lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Hi. I'm Arnold Grumbel, of Grumbel's Ladders. For eleven generations, my family has made ladders that go up.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: But not every move in life is up. Sometimes you need to go sideways. A new job, at the same level. A new flat, on the same floor. Next door, but nicer.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: So we made the Lateral. It's a ladder, on its side. You walk across it.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. So is sideways.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Have you climbed too high? Said yes to everything, and now you're up there, and it's windy?

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: The Grumbel's Down Ladder only goes one way, and it goes gently. One rung at a time, back to where your feet are.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: There's no shame in coming down. My grandfather came down from the very top at ninety. He said the view from the bottom was better, because it had his family in it.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Not every dream is a big dream. Some dreams are the top shelf.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: For those, there's the Grumbel's Step Stool. Two rungs. Very stable. It gets you to the biscuits and back, and it never once asks you why.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. A little bit up is still up.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Introducing the Ambition, from Grumbel's Ladders. The ladder with no top.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Our test climber has been going for three years. Last month's postcard said, nice view, still going. This month's said, I can see everyone's house. Please tell my mother.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Ambition. For people who don't want to arrive. Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders cannot guarantee a top, a bottom, or your mother.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Breaking in new shoes? Don't. Wear Someone Else's Shoes.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Every pair is pre-worn by a version of you from the next reality over. He walked the dog. He took the long way home. He never once stepped in anything. He is, frankly, a better you than you.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Walk a mile in his shoes. It's easier than you'd think. He's already done it.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Someone Else's Shoes. Slightly used. By you.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Can't sleep? Try Yesterday Night. The sleep aid you take today, so that you slept well last night.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Wake up rested, refreshed, and with a faint memory of a lovely dream about a boat.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Do not operate heavy machinery yesterday. Yesterday Night may cause drowsiness last week. If you have already slept, please consult your past.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: In the Damp Dimension, the rain falls down. And on Thursdays, it falls up.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: You need a Gilroy's Double Umbrella. One on top, one underneath, and you in the middle, perfectly dry, like the filling in a very sensible sandwich.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Gilroy's Umbrellas. Four thousand years of keeping Precinct Nine dry. Well. Drier.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Lunar Laundrette, Tranquility Base Annex.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: One wash takes twenty nine days, one full turn of the moon. Your socks come back clean, and a little bit wiser.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Low gravity means low wrinkles. Your shirts simply float dry.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: And while you wait, there's a cafe next door. The coffee comes with an echo.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Lunar Laundrette. Bring a book. Bring several.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: For the discerning robot. Fennimore's Fine Oils.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Our oils will not give you feelings. Nothing can. But they will make the absence of feelings squeak considerably less.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Lavender, for the joints. Sandalwood, for the servos. And for the harpsichordist who has everything, a lightly scented valve oil, with notes of regret.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Fennimore's. Adequately moving.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Game over? Not with Spare Continue Insurance!

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: For a low monthly fee, we'll keep a spare continue in our vault, just for you. Run out of lives? Call us. We'll put the coin in.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Spare Continue Insurance. Because everybody deserves one more go.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Continues do not include extra lives. Extra lives sold separately. Player Two is still waiting, and has asked us to say, any time now.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Need a holiday that comes back around? Book a week at Perihelion Point, the only resort on the tail of a comet!

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: White sands! Warm stars! A pool with no water in it, because it's in space, but a lovely view of the pool!

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: And because we pass the sun every seventy six years, your holiday comes around again, whether you like it or not!

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: The return journey is the same journey. Pack light. Pack for seventy six years.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Is your reflection doing its own thing? Waving when you're not? Leaving the room before you do? Call Reflection Repair.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Our trained technicians will have a quiet word with it. Most reflections just want to be listened to.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Reflection Repair. We'll get you back in step. Or at least, in the same step, half a second apart.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Slow Mail. Post, delivered by snail.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Every letter is carried by hand. Well. By foot. Well. By a snail, at a steady and dignified pace.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Birthday cards arrive in time for the next birthday. Love letters arrive when you've both had time to think about it.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Slow Mail. Guaranteed.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Eventually.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Can't relax? Try the Distant Dishwasher. The sleep machine that plays the reassuring sound of someone else, somewhere in the house, doing the chores.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Choose from a dishwasher, a washing machine on its final spin, or somebody's dad, quietly drying up, and humming.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Distant Dishwasher. Somebody's taking care of it. Go to sleep.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Running out of week? Keep a Spare Tuesday in the glovebox.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: It fits most weeks. Pops in between Monday and Wednesday, and nobody notices. Use it to catch up, or to lie down, or to finally ring your sister back.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Spare Tuesday. For emergencies, and for Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: The Spare Tuesday is temporary and should not be used as a regular day. Do not use the Spare Tuesday on a Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Not sure about something? Call the Second Opinion Hotline. Whatever you've decided, a friendly voice will gently disagree.

lines.speaker: Second Opinion Hotline
lines.text: Hello, second opinion. Mm. Have you thought about the blue one?

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Press one to be told you're probably right. Press two to be told you should sleep on it. Press three to be told there's no rush. There's never a rush.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Stuck indoors? Nowhere to stare? Carry a Pocket Horizon.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Unfold it on any desk, and there it is. A long, flat, distant line between the sky and everything else. Gaze at it. Think about your life. Feel like somebody in a film.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Pocket Horizon. Now available in sunset. Sunrise has sold out. People get up early for sunrise.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Nobody's Bakery. Bread that nobody made.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: We don't know where it comes from. Every morning, there it is, on the shelves. Warm. Perfect. With a little crust that sings when you squeeze it.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: We've stopped asking. You should too.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Nobody's Bakery. Open from whenever, until it's gone.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: They're all in the same place, you know. Every odd sock you've ever lost is in the same dimension. A warm, quiet one. Honestly, they're very happy there.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: We go and get them anyway. The Sock Recovery Institute. We bring them back washed, paired, and only a little bit homesick.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Socks may not wish to return. Socks may return with a new partner. Please be supportive.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Tired of noisy neighbors? Hire a Quiet Neighbor.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: We'll move in next door, and you will never hear a single sound from us. Not a footstep. Not a cough. Not a door. Ever.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: You'll wonder about us. You'll lie awake wondering. And that's a kind of company, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Quiet Neighbor Service. We're here. Probably.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Feeling heavy? Some days are like that. Try Gravity Lite.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: All of the down, about half of the pull. Your shopping feels lighter. Your stairs feel shorter. Your worries, technically, weigh less.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Gravity Lite. For days when you need the ground, but not quite so much of it.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Gravity Lite is not suitable for birds, balloons or anyone under four foot. Please keep one foot on the floor at all times.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Mornings too loud? Try the Polite Alarm Clock. It doesn't ring. It doesn't buzz. At the time you've chosen, it simply clears its throat.

lines.speaker: The Polite Alarm Clock
lines.text: Ahem. Sorry. It's seven.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: And if you don't get up, it says, no, you're right, five more minutes, and lets you be.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Polite Alarm Clock. Nobody ever got up faster for being shouted at.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Visit the Overlap! Where two realities meet, and both of them are lovely!

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Have breakfast in one world, and lunch in the other! See the famous Double Bridge, built by two engineers who never met, and agree on almost everything!

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Meet yourself at the market, and buy each other a coffee!

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Overlap. You'll want to come back. You may already be here.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: No time to wait? Hire a professional! At Queue Ahead, our trained waiters will stand in any queue, on your behalf, for as long as it takes.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Our senior waiter, Agatha, has been waiting since she was eleven. She is very, very good.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Queue Ahead. We wait, so you don't have to. Call now!

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: You will be put on hold.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Every year, when the clocks go forward, an hour goes missing. Where does it go? We know.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Lost Hour Recovery will track down your missing hour and return it to you, in a plain envelope, for use at your convenience.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Spend it on a walk. Spend it asleep. Spend it doing absolutely nothing, which, let's be honest, is what you'd have done with it anyway.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Recovered hours may be slightly used. Hours lost before the age of ten cannot be recovered. They were well spent.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Said something you regret? Press the Unsend Button.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Your words come back out of the air, fold themselves up, and go quietly back into your mouth, as though nothing had happened.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Perfect for meetings, dinners, and the end of long phone calls with your brother.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: The Unsend Button does not work on things you meant.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Owe geese? Of course you do. Geese Express delivers.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Seven, seven, four geese, to any radio mast, by morning. Calm, counted, and wearing a little bow.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Settle your account, and sleep at night again. Geese Express.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Geese Express does not deliver ducks. If you were asked for ducks, please listen again.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: A message from the Multiverse Broadcast Authority.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: If you find a shadow without a person, please do not step on it. Do not fold it. Do not try it on. Shadows are not lost property. They are on a journey. Leave a light on, and let it decide.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: If the shadow answers to Greg, his person, Hollis, would like you to know the porch light is on.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: The Multiverse Broadcast Authority reminds listeners that if you hear a voice between stations, asking whether anyone can hear them, it is polite to say yes.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: You don't have to say anything else. Yes is plenty.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: If you believe you may owe the Numbers Station geese, please don't panic. Have your geese ready, and calm.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Do not send ducks. Do not send swans. It isn't the same, and the swans don't like it.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: This has been a message from the Office of Fair Geese.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Tonight, all clocks in the Overlap go back one hour. Please do not go back with them.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Last year, several people did. They're having a lovely time, but they've missed a lot.

clips.title: A Message from Your Future Self

lines.speaker: Your Future Self
lines.text: Hi. This message is brought to you by your future self.

lines.speaker: Your Future Self
lines.text: We'd like you to drink a glass of water. We're very busy and don't have time to explain. Just the water, please.

lines.speaker: Your Future Self
lines.text: Thank you. You'll thank us. Well. You'll thank you.

clips.title: Please Do Not Feed the Void

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Please do not feed the void. It doesn't need it, and it only encourages it.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: If the void follows you home, do not make eye contact. Let it study. It has exams.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: A reminder from the Multiverse Broadcast Authority. The static between stations is not dangerous.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: It is just everybody else, talking at once. If you listen carefully, some of it is about you. Most of it is nice.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Check on your neighbors this winter. The ones upstairs, the ones downstairs, and the ones in the walls.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Especially the ones in the walls. Nobody ever checks on them. A small knock is fine. They'll knock back.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Lost something? Before contacting the authorities, please check under the sofa, then the other dimension, then under the sofa again.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: Ninety percent of lost items are found under the sofa. The rest are having a nice time elsewhere.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The sun has been working very hard this week. It comes up every single morning, and nobody ever asks how it's doing.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: If you see it today, give it a wave. It can't wave back. It hasn't got hands. But it'll know.

clips.title: You Are Allowed to Hang Up

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Hello, love. Grenda here, from ninety seven point eight, with a little reminder.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You're allowed to hang up on a problem. If it's serious, it'll ring back. And if you need someone to talk to in the meantime, the kettle's on.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Is anyone receiving this. This is Relay Four.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: If you can hear me, the kettle's on.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Relay Four. Still here. Still listening. Hello to whoever has the volume up.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: This is Relay Four. Is anyone receiving—

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello? Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Yes. Yes it is.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello? Is this the request line? It goes dum, dum—

lines.speaker: Emergency Broadcast System
lines.text: This is a test of the Interdimensional Emergency Broadcast System. If this had been an actual emergency, you would have heard about it yesterday.

lines.speaker: Emergency Broadcast System
lines.text: This has been a test. You passed. Barely. We are very proud of you.

lines.speaker: Dale Quarterly
lines.text: And the moon continues to look near you. More at eleven. It is always eleven.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And he's scored into last season! Last season is furious!

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's what leaving feels like, love. Both is exactly right.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: Greg, if you're listening. You don't have to come back. But the porch light's on.

lines.speaker: Numbers Station
lines.text: Seven. Seven. Four. Seven. Seven. Four.

lines.speaker: Numbers Station
lines.text: Geese.

lines.speaker: A Faint Voice
lines.text: Is anyone else hearing this? Or is it just me?

lines.speaker: A Faint Voice
lines.text: Oh, good.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: We interrupt this broadcast to say, you're doing fine. That's all. Back to the music.

lines.speaker: Darlene, the Everything Channel
lines.text: And it comes in oak, pine, or regret.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Music may contain feelings. Feelings not included. If symptoms persist, please consult your nearest Linda.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: It's Halloween. You've heard something in the attic. You've heard it every night this week. A sort of shuffle, and then a sigh.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: The Grumbel's Attic Ladder folds down quietly, takes your weight without a creak, and gets you up there in time to find out it's the water tank. It's always the water tank.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: My grandfather went up one Halloween and found a family of owls. He brought them down one rung at a time. Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. Even in the dark.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Is your house too quiet this Halloween? Rent a ghost for the season, from Haunt-a-Home Lettings.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Every ghost is vetted, polite, and only slightly see-through. They'll rattle a door, hum on the landing, and leave the good spoons alone.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Haunt-a-Home. Somebody's home. Sort of.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Ghost may become attached. Ghost may become attached to the house. Ghost may not wish to leave in November. Ghost is lovely, though.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Can't think of a costume? Wear Someone Else's Costume.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Every outfit has been pre-worn by a version of you from the next reality over, who had a brilliant idea, started early, and finished the sleeves.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: He went as a lighthouse. Everybody said so. He is, frankly, a better you than you, and this year, you can be him.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Someone Else's Costume. Slightly used. By you.

clips.title: The Polite Alarm Clock: Halloween Edition

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: This Halloween, wake up gently, with the Polite Alarm Clock, Halloween Edition.

lines.speaker: The Polite Alarm Clock
lines.text: Ahem. Sorry. Boo. It's seven.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: It's still the same clock. It still clears its throat. It's just wearing a very small sheet.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Polite Alarm Clock. Nobody ever got up faster for being frightened, either.

clips.title: The Sock Recovery Institute: The Night They Come Back

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Once a year, on Halloween night, they come back. Every sock you've ever lost returns to its drawer. Just for one night. To see how everyone's getting on.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Don't be frightened. Leave the drawer open a crack. They've missed you. They've missed the other one most of all.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: The Sock Recovery Institute. We bring them back the rest of the year, too.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Returning socks may be slightly warm, and may smell faintly of another dimension. This is normal. Please do not wear the visiting socks.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Halloween party lacking atmosphere? Uncork a bottle of genuine Overlap Fog.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Hand-gathered at dawn from the low-lying timelines, our fog rolls in under the door, settles round the ankles, and makes every guest look mysterious, even Gerald from accounts.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: Overlap Fog. You won't see the difference. You won't see much of anything.

lines.speaker: Small Print
lines.text: Fog may contain a bicycle. Fog may contain Skip Daley, who has been in there since Tuesday. Please send him back to the newsroom.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: The Multiverse Broadcast Authority reminds listeners that this week, the static between stations is a little louder than usual.

lines.speaker: Multiverse Broadcast Authority
lines.text: That is everybody who used to listen, listening in. Turn it up a bit. They like the music. They always did.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Relay Four. Happy Halloween, whoever you are. Captain has come dressed as a ghost.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: He's a white gull. It's not much of a costume.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: They're saying the dial's got longer. New stations, out past one hundred and eight, further than anyone's tuned before.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: The Grumbel's Outer Band Extension. Three extra rungs. Clips on to the top of any Grumbel's ladder, so you can hold your radio up that little bit higher, and listen.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: My grandfather heard the sea from the top of one. He lived nowhere near the sea. Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. Out is a bit further.
